title: Rav Avya
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was Rav Yosef’s student, as in Berakhot 28b: Rav Avya was ill and did not come to Rav Yosef’s lecture. The next day when he came, Abaye wanted to appease Rav Yosef’s mind; Abaye asked Rav Avya, “Why did the Master not come to the lecture?” He said to him, “My heart was weak,” etc. In Shabbat 148a: Rav Avya was sitting before Rav Yosef; his hand became dislocated (and it was Shabbat). He said to him, “What about like this?” “Forbidden.” “And like this?” “Forbidden.” Meanwhile his hand recovered. He said to him: “What is your question?”

In Ketubot 57a he came before Rav Yosef; in Beitzah 13b he spoke in Rav Yosef’s name; and they are likewise mentioned together in Shabbat 63a: “Abaye said to Rav Dimi — and some say to Rav Avya — and some say Rav Yosef to Rav Avya.”
Likewise Rabbah bar Rav Chanan was his colleague, as in Kiddushin 39a.

Hyman infers that he went up to the Land of Israel and was there a short time, as we find in Chullin 3a, where he said, “I was standing before Rabbi Ami … Rabbi Ami said”; and in Bava Kamma 35a, “Rav Avya said to Rabbi Abbahu.” Hyman infers from this that he went up to Caesarea at the end of Rabbi Ami’s days, where he founded his academy; but afterward he went down to Babylonia, possibly with all the nechotei (those who went down [to Babylonia]). This is what we find in Eruvin 120a: “Rav Avya visited Nehardea”; and in Shabbat 46a: Rav Avya visited Rabbah’s house; his shoes were soiled with mud; he sat on the bed before Rava, and Rava was annoyed. Rava wanted to distress him and asked him, but he answered properly, and Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: “Blessed is the Merciful One, that Rava did not shame him.” (Hyman argues: The scholars of our time found room to distinguish themselves by saying: See how a Torah scholar like Rav Avya had no manners and soiled Rava’s bed, until Rava was annoyed with him; and from this, that Rava loved cleanliness. But in truth there was neither bear nor forest for one who examines there, for the incident was on Shabbat, and Rava holds there that it is permitted to wipe with a potsherd even in a public domain, while Rav Avya holds that it is forbidden; when he came before Rava with soiled shoes, Rava showed him from the law of Rabbah and Rav Yosef, who said that a naphtha lamp too may be moved; and he answered him properly.) Of his personal history we find in Bava Batra 100b that his wife was the sister of Rami bar Pappa, and she died and he made a ceremony of standing and sitting for her; and Rav Yosef said he erred in two things … and Abaye said he erred in this too … and Rava said he erred in this too. In Ketubot 56b [it is related] that he married the sister of Rami bar Chama (and possibly it is corrupted in one of the [two] places), and her ketubah was lost, and they came to Rav Yosef [to ask] what to do. His sayings we find in Shabbat 23a, Megillah 17a and Bava Batra 143a; in Menachot 43a, “Rav Ada [bar Abba] before Rava in the name of Rav Avira [Hyman, citing Dikdukei Soferim, proposes Avya]”; and in Bava Batra 143a, “Rav Mordekhai said to Rav Ashi: Rav Avya raised a refutation.” We find Rav Ada son of Rav Avya, Bava Kamma 62a; Rav Huna bar Avya, Bava Batra 143a; Huna Mar bar Avya, Chullin 47a; Rav Chilkiyah son of Rav Avya (in Rava’s time), Bava Metzia 96b; and Rav Acha son of Rav Avya, Eruvin 11b.

notes.text: Hyman’s travel chronology, Caesarea inference and polemical defense remain attributed to him. The supplied wording attaches the academy phrase to Rabbi Ami; the old draft’s inserted Rabbi Abbahu has been removed rather than quietly altering that antecedent. Berakhot28b’s whole saved Davidson paragraph shows Abaye questioning Avya to appease Yosef. להתגדר means to distinguish themselves, not make a fence; קורותיו concerns personal history; במק״א means one of the two places; נחותי are the sages descending from the Land of Israel to Babylonia. The wife’s Rami bar Pappa/bar Chama discrepancy and Hyman’s proposed corruption remain explicit. Source Eruvinקכ. is120a; saved Davidson102a contains Avya’s Nehardea visit. Source Shabbat46a alternates Rabbah/Rava, while the saved named Davidson paragraph has Rava as host and Rabbah together with Rav Yosef in the lamp ruling. This supports the comparison but no printing-history claim. לא יער ולא דובים is Hyman’s literal neither forest nor bears idiom, meaning no basis for that claim.

The consulted Berakhot 28b has Abaye questioning Avya to appease Yosef. Shabbat 46a names Rava as host and Rabbah with Rav Yosef in the lamp ruling; Hyman’s Rabbah/Rava alternation remains visible. Eruvin 102a directly names Avya’s Nehardea visit beside Hyman’s supplied 120a. His short migration, Caesarea academy antecedent and polemical defense remain his own reconstruction; no new Abbahu antecedent is inserted. The Rami bar Pappa/bar Chama wife discrepancy and Avira/Avya correction remain explicit, and the list of sons called bar Avya is not proof that all share one father. Exact Dikdukei Soferim and printing-history claims have not been inspected here.
